pr_title: Make ProgressBar reflect the real value in the percent label when "allow greater" is checked
pr_body:
Fix https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/63311.

I have just a question. When we change the `min value` or the `max value`, the `current value` is updated if it is above the `max value` or below the `min value`. Should I implement this behavior when the user toggles `Allow Greater/Lesser`? Right now if I toggle  `Allow Greater/Lesser` it will keep the old value, as you can see in the video below.


https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/22689195/1fe71355-de93-4533-9911-6e55d4e3d865

It seems because in the `Range` class it doesn't emit the change like the other properties (e.g.: `page`, `max`, `min`, `etc`.).

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/f8818f85e6c43cdf1277e8ae85eba19ca0a003b0/scene/gui/range.cpp#L360-L362
pr_comments: You can't just divide by max, you need to take min into account also avoid dividing by 0.

It was too good to be right on the first try haha. 

Now I just need to know if I need to fix the behavior that I mentioned in the video, or if it's expected.

It breaks `exp_edit` though:
![image](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/2223172/9d1662e8-c3b8-43cb-b8bb-0e5c95231807)
I think instead of inventing custom ratio, `get_as_ratio()` should be modified to allow values outside the 0-1 range if `allow_greater`/`allow_lesser` are enabled. The value is explicitly clamped, so it should be easy change.

> It seems because in the Range class it doesn't emit the change like the other properties

This is irrelevant, because changing these properties does not affect current value.

You're right, it would be much simpler, but I don't think we can do that safely, because some UI elements rely on the value from `get_as_ratio()`, and it will break if the value is outside of the 0-1 range, as you can see below:

![image](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/22689195/3d9e4fa6-46c0-4d4f-b901-0bee6d462089)

I just have one question, if the `exp_edit` and `allow_lesser` are checked what is the expected behavior if the `value` is less than or equal to 0?

> I just have one question, if the exp_edit and allow_lesser are checked what is the expected behavior if the value is less than or equal to 0?

`exp_edit` requires the min_value to be `>= 0`, so I think the exp ratio should be always 0 when below that.

btw "`exp_edit` requires the min_value to be `>= 0`," is not respected by your code. I think the implementation is ok, just make sure that the percentage always matches the filled bar, i.e. 50% should be when the bar is half filled etc. Right now it's still possible to desync it.

> [...] I think the implementation is ok, just make sure that the percentage always matches the filled bar, i.e. 50% should be when the bar is half filled etc. Right now it's still possible to desync it.

To be honest, I don't see how it could desync, because it's the same logic as the `get_as_ratio()`, do you have an example?

I tried to see if it behaved differently from the stable version, but I don't see the difference, as you can see below (I tried some different values too).

### Godot 4.1

![4 1](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/22689195/67d19479-fdf4-4961-afbe-99668339340c)

### This PR

![mine](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/22689195/757519b7-bd60-4fa6-919b-fe2b64c706a0)

Ok the only one I could find was with `exp_edit` (again xd) and negative `min_value`:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/2223172/2d1ba726-9847-4f51-83d6-493e4e11d6bf

Other than that the value displays correctly.
Now I think it works as expected.
Thanks, and congrats on your first merged Godot contribution!

issue_context.title: ProgressBar should reflect "allow greater" values in the percent label
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

v3.5.beta.custom_build [3c0d32562]

### System information

NixOS

### Issue description

`ProgressBar` currently doesn't reflect values that exceed `max_value` when `allow_greater = true`, while sibling `Range` descendant `SpinBox` does correctly display values above `max_value` in this scenario. Does it make sense for `ProgressBar`s to display >100% labels when `allow_greater = true` and `percent_visible = true` given that `value` is clamped to `max_value` when `allow_greater = false` anyway and this is a visual component not really meant as a data store? (the only scenario I can think of where clamping the label to "100%" when `allow_greater = true` is useful is when someone wants to use it as a data store)

Relevant code:

* `3c0d32562` (my build): https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/3c0d32562b558b60abe382f2a132f4ea0f25b380/scene/gui/progress_bar.cpp#L66
    * Specifically `get_as_ratio()` since it clamps between `min_value` and `max_value`, we probably just want a `value / max_value * 100` instead here.
* `master`: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/653f95282ccd31a4e38a157bb7845405079de371/scene/gui/progress_bar.cpp#L104

### Steps to reproduce

Set `allow_greater = true` and `value = 150` and the label doesn't match the value, it's clamped to "100%" despite `allow_greater = true`.

### Minimal reproduction project

_No response_
comments: I think allowing values larger than 100% to display makes sense, but make sure it doesn't mess up rounding when using large values. (In other words, "101%" shouldn't display when the value is actually 100% with large maximum value.)

review_comments: Maybe it's worth it to add a comment that it's basically copy-paste of `get_as_ratio()`, but unclamped.
